What comes up in Greenacre

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. This sets out the typical case here rather than anything about a given address.

Secondary dwelling site clearance

Greenacre blocks were laid out for one dwelling and are now carrying two or three, which puts the services and the boundaries ahead of the demolition.

How it is handled
Disconnections confirmed in writing, the existing dwelling and rear structures removed, then the block left level to the new set out.
What does it
Midi excavator with a grapple, with tippers for the smaller volumes.

Rear yard structures and the slab beneath them

Sheds, garages and old concrete that have to come out before a second dwelling can be sited.

How it is handled
Structures taken down and separated by stream, then the slab broken out where the new design needs the ground back.
What does it
Mini or midi excavator with a hammer, and a grading bucket to finish the level.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Greenacre

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Duplex and secondary dwelling conversion The dominant job type, and it brings services, easements and boundaries forward before anything is demolished.
  • Original single dwelling blocks Which means one set of services for what will become two or three dwellings, and that has to be sorted first.
  • Rear yard structures Sheds, garages and occasionally a pool, each with its own waste stream.
  • Pre 1990 construction With bonded asbestos assumed until tested.

Greenacre blocks are generally regular with usable side access, and the streets take tippers without difficulty. The complications here are more often in the paperwork than in the plant: on a multi dwelling conversion, the disconnections and the approval conditions set the start date.

Greenacre questions

What people ask before we start

Do the services need disconnecting before demolition?
Yes, and in writing. Water, sewer, gas, electricity and telecommunications all have to be confirmed as disconnected before a structure comes down, and on a multi dwelling site that is usually the longest lead item.
Can you demolish the house and leave the garage?
Yes. Partial demolition is routine, and the garage is retained, protected and left weatherproof rather than simply avoided.
Can one contractor do the demolition, the asbestos and the dig?
Yes, and across Western Sydney that is how most jobs run. The asbestos is removed and cleared first, the structure comes down, the site cut follows and the spoil is carted on the same contract, which means one set of truck movements planned once.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
